answer: An economy can resist clones by tying each identity to a hollow vial it keeps. The registry fills it with a unique isotope blend, seals it with a lotus-etched cap, and records its ripple trace, a fingerprint no other vial shares. Each epoch the holder presents the vial for assay; decay moves the trace along a curve, so a copied or refilled vial fails. Each assay consumes a sample and keys the next to its result, so assays run in sequence and one vial cannot serve two identities. A fake costs $380 in blend and assay fees; ten thousand fakes cost $3,800,000, and no bulk order duplicates a trace.
